db_evidence.notes: The clue interval (34020-34127s) IS present in the memory DB: episodes/topic_facts rows describe the player reaching a shrine ('character reaches the shrine, a chinese-language interaction menu appears offering options such as resting and saving'), opening the talent screen (本事/根器/神通, 23/37, 32/57), then browsing the 奇术 tab where nodes under 定身法 and 安身法 branches are confirmed with '已升级'/'已消耗无尤人'. Manual frame inspection (memcli frame at 34119-34135s) confirms a node whose info panel reads '假借须臾' is highlighted and taken through the hold-to-confirm ('长按参悟') gesture with a currency counter showing 3/2, matching the reference answer 'Borrow a Moment' (假借须臾 = literally 'borrow[ing] an instant/moment'). However, the auto-generated episode caption for this exact window mis-OCR's the node name as '银精须臾' (a plausible-looking but wrong reading), which would mislead any text-only retrieval. The keyword 'meditation point' itself only appears verbatim in the DB once, at 2820s (chapter 1, event_steps:00000101/00014678), and is never applied to the shrine visit inside the true clue window, so keyword search for 'meditation point' cannot find the clue at all. Chapter labeling is also genuinely ambiguous in the DB: '第三回' chapter-title cards recur at 21420s, 21720s, and 44250s, and a separate auto-caption at 63120s claims the player 'confirms entry into chapter 3' after a different, unrelated talent upgrade -- a strong, semantically on-topic but likely mislabeled distractor that pulled one rollout far outside the correct chapter span entirely.

root_causes: Vocabulary mismatch: the question's phrase 'meditation point' does not consistently appear in the DB's captions for the actual shrine visit in the clue window (captions instead say 'resting and saving', 'interaction menu', 'shrine'); the one literal 'meditation point' hit in the DB is an unrelated chapter-1 event, so keyword and embedding search for 'meditation point' never surfaces the true 34020-34140s window.

Ambiguous/duplicated chapter boundaries: multiple DB rows independently claim 'chapter 3' status at different times (21420s, 21720s, 44250s, and a conflicting 63120s auto-caption), so agents anchor on different, sometimes very distant, candidate spans without reconciling which one is authoritative.

No agent actually performed the 'count shrine/meditation-point visits and take the 4th' step explicitly; even the two rollouts (3 and 4) whose SQL scans did include or nearly include the correct window picked a different, later confirmed-talent-upgrade event in the same chapter rather than systematically enumerating all shrine visits in order.

OCR/captioning error on the correct clue frame itself: the episode caption in the true window reads the talent name as '银精须臾' instead of the ground-truth '假借须臾' visible in frames, so even an agent that reached this exact interval via text search alone (without clip_qa) would have derived a wrong Chinese name and, consequently, a wrong English translation.

All 5 rollouts stopped after one clip_qa confirmation on a plausible-looking talent-upgrade scene rather than cross-checking that scene followed exactly the 4th, not some other-numbered, meditation point in chapter 3.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly followed the general-retrieval -> locating-time-intervals -> semantic-search/sql-schema -> visual-verification skill sequence and used clip_qa to visually confirm a candidate talent-upgrade event before submitting, rather than guessing from text alone.

Rollout 3's broad, unfiltered SQL scan across the full 21000-44600s chapter span is the correct general strategy for this kind of 'find the Nth event of type X' question, and it did pull in the true clue-window rows as raw data (even though the agent did not act on them).
transferable_lessons: For 'the Nth <landmark> in <chapter>' questions, do a systematic ordered enumeration (SQL over a broad time range, sorted by time, filtered loosely e.g. by 'shrine'/'rest'/'save'/'meditat' OR-ed together) and explicitly count occurrences to identify the Nth one, rather than trusting semantic_search to land on the right ordinal instance -- semantic/embedding search tends to return the single most 'typical'-looking match, not the correct ordinal occurrence.

Do not trust a single auto-caption's claim of 'chapter N' at face value, especially if it conflicts with earlier chapter-title cards already seen in the DB; when multiple 'chapter 3' labels exist, prefer the one anchored to an explicit title-card cutscene (e.g. '第三回 ... ' fading in) over a narrative aside embedded in a caption about an unrelated action.

When the question's landmark term (e.g. 'meditation point') doesn't appear verbatim in captions, broaden the query with domain-specific synonyms actually used by this game's UI (shrine, rest, save, campfire, checkpoint) and cross-check against event_steps 'interaction menu' phrasing rather than relying on the literal phrase.

OCR of on-screen Chinese talent names in auto-captions can be wrong even when superficially plausible (e.g. 银精须臾 vs the true 假借须臾); when the answer hinges on an exact proper-noun read from a screen, always verify with clip_qa/frame extraction at the precise decisive second rather than trusting the episode-level caption text.

After a clip_qa visual confirmation, sanity-check that the confirmed event is preceded by the correct count of the anchor landmark (here: literally counting shrine visits from the start of the chapter) before submitting -- a visually-confirmed but mis-ordinal event is still a wrong answer.
open_questions: Whether the true 4th-meditation-point count is itself unambiguous given the DB's ambiguous chapter boundaries -- I did not exhaustively enumerate every shrine/rest visit between 21420s (first '第三回' title) and 34020s to independently verify '4th', so it remains possible the reference answer's own chapter/ordinal framing relies on ground-truth game knowledge not fully recoverable from this DB.

Whether '假借须臾' is the officially localized in-game English name 'Borrow a Moment', or whether the reference answer was derived from an external walkthrough/wiki rather than purely from this video; I inferred the translation from the literal characters (假借 = borrow/pretend, 须臾 = a moment) and the visual confirm-gesture, not from an authoritative in-game English-localization string found in the DB.
